questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about the characteristic features of the Indian Desert?

options.text: It is also known as Marusthali.
It lies northwest of the Aravalli hills.
It receives 250 mm rainfall per year.

questions.solution:
The current answer is __**It receives 250 mm rainfall per year**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The defining characteristics of the** Indian Desert** include its vast expanse of **sand dunes and an annual rainfall of less than 150 mm**. 
 
• Situated between the** Aravalli Mountains** and the plains formed by the **Sutlej and Indus rivers**, it's also known as the **Thar Desert**. 
 
• Comprised mainly of rocks and sand, it exhibits a harsh, dry climate, with temperatures ranging from near freezing to a** scorching 50°C**. 
 
• Despite the challenging conditions, some areas experience a fleeting spring season. 
 
• This region, although densely populated, presents a formidable environment for human, plant, and animal survival compared to other landscapes. 
 
• Millet stands out as the primary crop cultivated in the Indian Desert.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Thar Desert, **also referred to as the** Great Indian Desert,** sprawls across the north-western region of the Indian subcontinent, spanning approximately 200,000 km² (77,000 sq mi) across India and Pakistan.
 
• Ranking as the **18th largest desert **globally and the 9th largest hot subtropical desert, it boasts an arid and subtropical climate.
 
• Temperature fluctuations are notable between seasons, ranging from near-freezing in winter to over 50°C during the summer months.
 
• Annual rainfall averages between 100 to 500 mm, primarily occurring in the brief July-to-September southwest monsoon period.
 
• The desert comprises a distinctly dry area, Marusthali, in the west, contrasted by a semidesert section in the east, characterized by fewer sand dunes and slightly increased precipitation.

questions.question: In which of the following states is the Tamu Lachar festival celebrated as the New Year by the Gurung Community?
questions.solution:

• **Sikkim** observes the **Tamu Lochar festival, **which is the** New Year celebration of the Gurung community,** on** December 30th **annually.
 
• This festival signifies the transition of the** animal sign (lho) for the Gurung people.**
 
• **Tamu Lochar **stands as a significant festival for the Hindu Nepalese community in Sikkim, believed to have ancient origins predating Buddhism in the region.
 
• Festivities include elaborate feasts featuring traditional Gurung cuisine and the exchange of warm greetings among individuals.
 
• Primarily celebrated by Nepalese Buddhists, particularly the Gurung ethnic group, the festival is centered around monasteries.

• As one of the prominent Gurkha tribes, they are estimated to comprise around 200,000 individuals.
 
• Primarily situated on the southern side of the Annapūrna mountain massif, the Gurung predominantly inhabit districts such as Manang, Mustang, Dolpo, Kaski, Lamjung, Gorkha, Parbat, Tanahun, and Syangja.
 
• Speaking a Tibeto-Burman language, the Gurung community is largely followers of Lamaist Buddhism, although some have embraced Hinduism.
 
• They possess a vibrant cultural heritage, characterized by a rich tradition of folk music and dance, which holds significant importance in their cultural practices.

questions.question: In 1948, Ernest Mackay mentioned that in the Harappan city of Lothal, the drains for the drainage system were made of _______ bricks.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**burnt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **1948, Ernest Mackay **mentioned that in the **Harappan city of Lothal**, the drains for the drainage system were made of **burnt bricks**.
 
• **Ernest Mackay's **findings on the drainage system in Lothal reveal the advanced urban planning and engineering skills of the **ancient Harappan civilization.**
 
• The drains, constructed with burnt bricks and mortar, were meticulously crafted with smooth, seamless joints.
 
• They featured removable bricks for easy cleaning, along with drops at regular intervals to facilitate automatic cleaning.
 
• This systematic approach demonstrated the Harappans' sophisticated understanding of sanitation and urban infrastructure, showcasing their remarkable organizational abilities and technological prowess.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **The Election Commission of India (ECI) **underwent a structural change from being a single-member body, with only the **Chief Election Commissioner,** from its establishment in **1950 until October 1989.**
 
• Following the **Election Commissioner Amendment Act 1989**, it evolved into a multi-member body.
 
• Since October 1989 to the present day, it has comprised three members: **one Chief Election Commissioner and two election commissioners.**

• Thus, the Election Commission functions as an all-India body, overseeing elections at both the central and state levels.
 
• The commission administers elections for various bodies, including the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies, State Legislative Councils, and the offices of the President and Vice President.
 
• Operating under the authority of the Constitution, as per Article 324, it is further guided by the Representation of the People Act.

questions.question: Pottery was first traceable to which period of ancient Indian history?

• This ancient craft is among the oldest human inventions, dating back thousands of years.

• These algae often form masses that float near the surface of streams and ponds, buoyed by oxygen bubbles produced during photosynthesis.
 
• They are frequently employed in laboratory demonstrations. Spirogyra species reproduce both sexually and asexually.

Radius = 4 cm

The cost of painting with blue is ₹2/cm2

Concept

When the sphere is halved, the total surface area gets increased.

The curved surface area of the hemisphere = 2πr2

Calculation

The curved surface area which is painted red and green = 2 * 2πr2

The cost of painting the curved area is ₹3/cm2 = 3 * 2 * 2πr2

⇒ 12πr2

Two new bases of both the hemispheres are to be painted with blue colour = 2 * πr2

The cost of painting with blue is ₹2/cm2 = 2 * 2 * πr2

⇒ 4πr2

The cost (in ₹) of painting the hemispheres = 12πr2 + 4πr2

⇒ 16πr2 → 16 * 3.14 * 16

⇒ ₹803.84

The cost (in ₹) of painting the hemispheres = ₹803.84
